backups.title: Backups
backups.description: Restore points of this server: write one now, upload one, download them, or take the server back to one.
backups.notEncrypted: Backups are not encrypted (the keys that protect sign-ins are left out of them)
backups.photosLeftOut: left out (they are in a folder of their own; see Backups:Photos)
backups.retention: After each backup the app writes, it keeps {{limits}}; the newest always stays
backups.runHint: The server writes the backup into its folder in the background; you can leave this page meanwhile.
backups.uploadHint: A backup of another server, or one you downloaded earlier, up to {{max}} MB. A larger file can be copied into the backups folder instead.
backups.pointsHint: Every backup in the folder is listed, also one copied in by hand. Restoring one replaces all data on this server.
backups.none: There are no backups in the folder yet. Back up now, upload one, or copy a file into {{folder}}.
backups.kindBackup: Backup (written by the app or copied into the folder)
backups.safetyNet: Safety net, written just before a database upgrade
backups.encryptedOther: Encrypted for another key: only that key set's passphrase opens it
backups.otherMigration: Made by a newer release: restore it with Tankstat {{version}} or later.
backups.olderMigration: Holds the database as an older release left it: brought up to date as it is restored.
backups.deleteDescription: The file is removed from the backups folder for good; the server cannot be taken back to it any more.
backups.restoreDescription: All data on this server is replaced by this backup: users, vehicles, logs and pictures. Whatever changed since it was made is lost: no backup of the current state is written. The app restarts to do it, which takes a moment for everyone using it.
backups.restoreOlder: It holds the database as an older release left it (the file was written by Tankstat {{version}}): the database is set up as that release left it, the backup loaded, and everything brought up to date, as an upgrade would. Once the old tables are removed this cannot be taken back.
backups.passphraseHint: The passphrase the backup's key was made from.
backups.identityHint: The line that starts with AGE-SECRET-KEY-1.
backups.restarting: Restoring the backup of {{made}}: the server is restarting. This page reloads by itself once it is back.
backups.restartSlow: This takes longer than usual. A server that is not started again by itself (by a restart policy or a service manager) has to be started by hand; its log says how the restore went.
backups.notRestored: The server is back, but the backup was not restored. Its log says why; the backups folder holds what was refused.
backups.encryptionOff: Backups are written without encryption. With a key set, they are encrypted and hold the keys that protect sign-ins too, so a restored server keeps everyone signed in.
backups.encryptionOn: Backups are encrypted for {{recipient}}. A new key set applies once it is used for new backups.
backups.keysTitle: A key set for encrypted backups
backups.keysDescription: The server makes the key from a passphrase, yours or one it makes up. The passphrase is stored nowhere: only the recipient and the salt are kept, once you use the keys for new backups.
backups.keysReplacing: Backups are already encrypted. Older backups still open only with their own passphrase.
backups.newPassphraseHint: At least {{min}} characters. Leave both empty and one is made up for you, which you type back once it is shown.
backups.typeBackHint: The made-up passphrase above, as you wrote it down: Use these keys for new backups is available once it matches.
backups.keysOnce: Write the passphrase down and keep it away from the server: no encrypted backup opens without it (or the identity). It is shown only now.
backups.keysUse: Use these keys for new backups
backups.keysInUse: Saved on the server: every backup from now on is encrypted with these keys.
backups.keysSettings: Or set these two settings in the server's environment, where they win over the settings page:
backups.keysSaved: I have kept the passphrase in a safe place
backups.changeSettings: Change the schedule, retention and encryption in the server settings
backups.environmentRecord: named in every backup; a restore elsewhere needs them set there
backups.environmentMerge: merged into every backup's settings file (secrets only with secrets in backups on)
backups.settingsBrings: It brings its server's settings file, which replaces this server's (kept as settings.json.bak). This server keeps its own database, folders and keys settings, and its passwords when the backup is not encrypted.
backups.environmentRecorded: Its server's environment set {{names}}. Their values are not in the backup: this server must set them.
backups.environmentMerged: Its server's environment set {{names}}. Their values are in its settings file (the secrets only if its server put them into its backups).

missing.text: The restore will be refused: its server set {{names}} in its environment, and this server sets none of them, nor does the backup's settings file hold them. Set them in this server's environment first.

mayBeMissing.short: May be refused: {{names}} not set here
mayBeMissing.text: Its server set {{names}} in its environment, which this server does not set. The backup is encrypted, so its settings file is read only with its passphrase: if it holds none of them, the restore will be refused.

logLevelsMissing.text: Its server set the log levels {{names}} in its environment, which this server does not set: the restore goes on, and the log holds what this server's levels say.

noSettingsOlder.short: No settings file (an older release wrote it)
noSettingsOlder.text: It holds no settings file and says nothing of its server's environment: a release before backups held them wrote it. This server's settings stay, which may not suit the restored data: its sign-in, its e-mail, its backups.

noSettingsNone.short: No settings file (its server had none)
noSettingsNone.text: Its server had no settings file, so the backup holds none. This server's settings stay, which may not suit the restored data: its sign-in, its e-mail, its backups.

noSettingsIgnored.short: No settings file (its server ran without it)
noSettingsIgnored.text: Its server ran without its settings file (its start left the file out), so the backup holds none. This server's settings stay, which may not suit the restored data.

secretsLeftOut.text: Its secrets are not in it ({{names}}): its server did not put them into its backups. This server keeps its own; what this server has none of stops working (the e-mail, the sign-in provider, photo reading).

signInOverridden.text: This server's environment sets the sign-in mode, which wins over the backup's. If they differ, the restored users may have no way to sign in (accounts of an identity provider have no password here, and the other way round).

overridden.text: This server's environment overrides {{names}}, which the backup's settings file holds: this server's values run, not the backup's.

environmentUnknown.short: Says nothing of its server's environment
environmentUnknown.text: It says nothing of the settings its server took from its environment (an older release wrote it): any of them may be missing here.

backups.risksTitle: What this restore can break here
backups.risksAcknowledge: I understand that the restored server may not work as before, and I want to restore it anyway.
backups.refusedNote: Set what is missing first: the server refuses this restore until then.
backups.secretsLeftOut: left out (a restore keeps the restored server's own)
backups.secretsIncludedPlain: included IN PLAIN: anyone with a backup file reads them
backups.held: Held: never removed by retention, not deleted until released
backups.heldSince: Held since {{since}}: never removed by retention, not deleted until released
backups.heldToast: {{file}} is held: retention keeps it, and it counts towards no limit.
backups.releasedToast: {{file}} was released: retention treats it like any other backup.
backups.deleteHeld: Held: release it to delete it
backups.secretsPlainMark: In plain with its secrets: anyone who has the file reads the passwords in it

groupHelp.DEFAULTS: What a new vehicle and a new schedule start with (every vehicle and schedule keeps its own values), and how times and dates are written for everyone who chose no format.
groupHelp.NOTIFICATIONS: How many notifications about events a person gets in an hour, and how long read ones are kept.
groupHelp.SYNC: How long the server remembers the changes devices sent and what was removed for good, for devices that keep data for offline use.
groupHelp.PHOTO_READING: A vision model behind an OpenAI-compatible API that reads receipts and dashboards; off without a provider. A cloud address sends every photo there.
groupHelp.BACKUPS: When backups are written on their own, how many are kept, what goes in and how they are encrypted. Backing up, uploading and restoring are on the Backups page.
groupHelp.LOGGING: The log level per category. The ASP.NET Core categories never go below Warning: their request lines hold the tokens of password reset links.
groupHelp.TELEMETRY: Traces, metrics and logs sent over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) to a collector or backend you choose; off without an endpoint. Like the log, what is sent holds ids, counts and reasons, never what someone typed, and never the one-time code.

help.Auth__Mode: How users sign in: None (no sign-in, everyone sees and changes everything), Standalone (accounts and passwords kept here), Oidc (an identity provider) or ProxyHeader (a trusted reverse proxy that signs users in).
help.Auth__PublicUrl: The address users open the app at, such as https://tankstat.example.com. Password links in e-mails start with it; required once a mail server and a sender are set.
help.Auth__AdminEmails: E-mail addresses or user names made administrators when they sign in through the provider or the proxy. It only promotes: taking the rights away is done on the Users page.
help.Auth__AccessTokenMinutes: How long the short sign-in cookie lasts (15 by default, 1 to 1440). A device still signed in gets a new one without asking.
help.Auth__RefreshTokenDays: How long a device stays signed in without being used (90 by default). Every use starts the period again.
help.Auth__RefreshRotationGraceSeconds: How long a refresh token already traded in is still accepted (60 by default), for tabs that refresh at the same moment.
help.Auth__Standalone__PasswordMinLength: The least a new password must have, from 10 to 128 characters (10 by default). It applies at once to every new password; existing passwords keep working.
help.Auth__Standalone__MaxFailedAttempts: Failed sign-ins before the account is locked (5 by default).
help.Auth__Standalone__LockoutMinutes: How long a locked account stays locked (15 by default).
help.Auth__Standalone__ResetTokenMinutes: How long a password setup or reset link works (60 by default, at most 30 days). Each link works once.
help.Auth__Standalone__ResetCooldownMinutes: After a link was sent, Forgot your password? sends no other for this long (5 by default, 0 turns it off), so nobody can flood a mailbox.
help.Auth__Standalone__AllowAdminSetPassword: Lets administrators set a user's password directly; the user is signed out everywhere. Off by default: administrators only issue reset links.
help.Auth__Oidc__Authority: The identity provider's issuer address, such as https://id.example.com. Its discovery document is checked before this is saved.
help.Auth__Oidc__ClientId: The client id this app is registered under at the provider.
help.Auth__Oidc__ClientSecret: The client secret the provider issued for this app. It is never shown back.
help.Auth__Oidc__Scopes: Extra scopes to ask the provider for, such as groups. openid, profile and email are always asked for.
help.Auth__ProxyHeader__UserHeader: The header the proxy puts the user name in (X-Forwarded-User by default).
help.Auth__ProxyHeader__EmailHeader: The header the proxy puts the user's e-mail address in (X-Forwarded-Email by default); empty to ignore it.
help.Auth__ProxyHeader__TrustedProxies: The addresses or ranges (such as 10.0.0.0/8) of the proxies whose headers are believed. At least one is needed; a request from anywhere else is not signed in.
help.Smtp__Host: The mail server that sends password setup and reset links. Without it (and a sender address), administrators hand links over themselves.
help.Smtp__Port: The mail server's port (587 by default; 465 for TLS from the start, 25 for plain).
help.Smtp__Username: The login at the mail server; empty to send without one.
help.Smtp__Password: The password of that login. It is never shown back.
help.Smtp__From: The address the e-mails come from.
help.Smtp__Security: How the connection to the mail server is secured. Auto (the default) picks by the port: TLS from the start on 465, otherwise STARTTLS when the server offers it.
help.Defaults__DistanceUnit: The distance unit a new vehicle starts with. Every vehicle keeps its own, and nothing is ever converted.
help.Defaults__VolumeUnit: The volume unit a new vehicle starts with.
help.Defaults__Currency: The currency a new vehicle's first log starts with, as a three-letter code such as EUR or HUF.
help.Defaults__RecurringWarnDays: How many days before it is due a new recurring expense starts warning (30 by default). Each schedule can change it.
help.Defaults__RecurringWarnDistance: How far before it is due, in the vehicle's distance unit, a new recurring expense starts warning (500 by default).
help.Defaults__TimeFormat: How times are written for everyone who has not chosen a format in the language menu: TwentyFourHour (13:29) or TwelveHour (1:29 PM). Not set: as each person's language writes them.
help.Defaults__DateFormat: How dates are written for everyone who has not chosen a format in the language menu: Iso (2026-10-13), DayMonthYearDots (13.10.2026), DayMonthYearSlashes (13/10/2026), MonthDayYear (10/13/2026) or YearMonthDayDots (2026. 10. 13.). Not set: as each person's language writes them.
help.Notifications__MaxPerHour: How many notifications about events a person gets in an hour (20 by default); further ones are only counted in one. Reminders do not count.
help.Notifications__ReadRetentionDays: How long a notification is kept after it was read (30 days by default). Unread ones are kept.
help.Sync__RetentionDays: How long the server remembers the changes devices sent, so a device that sends them again is told what happened instead of applying them twice.
help.Sync__TombstoneRetentionDays: How long the server remembers what was removed for good, so devices with offline data drop it too. A device away for longer downloads everything again.
help.Recognition__Provider: None (the default: photos are not read) or OpenAiCompatible: a vision model behind an OpenAI-compatible API reads receipts and dashboards.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__BaseUrl: The API's address including its version, such as http://ollama:11434/v1. A cloud address sends every photo there.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__Model: The model's name as the server lists it, such as qwen2.5vl:7b. Required.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__ApiKey: Sent as a Bearer token when set; a server on your own network usually needs none. It is never shown back.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__SystemPro: Your own instructions to the model instead of the built-in ones. What the model may answer is always sent as well.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__ResponseF: How the shape of the answer is enforced: JsonSchema (the default, for most servers), JsonObject for older ones, or None.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__Temperatu: Sent only when set (0 to 2). 0 makes a local model read the same digits the same way every time; some paid models refuse it.
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__TimeoutSe: How long one photo may take before the attempt counts as failed and is tried again later (120 by default).
help.Recognition__OpenAiCompatible__LogTraffi: Writes every request to the model server and every answer to the log, prompts and read values included. For finding out what goes wrong; off by default.
help.Recognition__MinConfidence: Values the model is less sure of than this are not filled in (0 to 1, 0.6 by default).
help.Recognition__MaxConcurrent: How many photos are read at the same time (2 by default; 1 for a single local GPU).
help.Backups__Every: One or more times of day such as 02:00, or 02:00, 14:00, in the server's time zone (TZ in a container): a backup is written then on each day chosen below, and one missed while the server was down is written when it starts. Empty: none are written on their own.
help.Backups__Days: The days of the week the times above apply to; every day by default. With no day ticked, none are written on their own.
help.Backups__Keep: After every backup the app writes, only this many of the newest files named tankstat-backup-… stay (the backup command's, and any copied in under that name, count too; the safety nets before upgrades are kept apart, the newest three); the newest is never removed. Uploads and files under another name are never counted. Empty: no limit by count.
help.Backups__KeepDays: After every backup the app writes, the files named tankstat-backup-… older than this many days are removed (the safety nets before upgrades are kept apart, the newest three); the newest always stays. Uploads and files under another name are never removed. Empty: no limit by age.
help.Backups__Photos: Only matters when the photos of logs have a folder of their own (Storage:PhotosPath): they grow without limit, so they are left out unless this is on. With one folder they are always in.
help.Backups__Environment: What a backup does with the settings environment variables hold here. Names only (Record): the backup names them, and a restore on a server where one of them has no value is refused until it is set. Names and values (Merge): the backup's copy of the settings file also takes the values this server runs with (never this server's own file), so a restore elsewhere brings them; the secrets only with Secrets in backups on.
help.Backups__Secrets: Every backup's settings file holds the secrets too (the OIDC client secret, the SMTP password, the model API key, the telemetry headers), so a restore elsewhere brings them. Off by default. In a backup that is not encrypted anyone who has the file reads them: make a key set on the Backups page to encrypt backups. With Names only (Settings from the environment), this is the only way the secrets in this server's settings file reach a backup; secrets held by environment variables travel only with Names and values. Either way a backup names every secret it leaves out.
help.Backups__Encryption__Recipient: The age recipient (age1…) backups are encrypted for. It and the salt are one pair, from one key set: make both with Make a key set on the Backups page and change them only together. Empty: backups are written in plain, without the keys that protect the sign-in.
help.Backups__Encryption__Salt: The salt the key is worked out from the passphrase with, printed with the recipient: the two belong together. With a salt of another key set (or one changed by hand) the passphrase no longer opens the backups written after it, only the identity does. Older backups keep their own passphrase.
help.Backups__PassphraseMinLength: The least a passphrase typed for encrypted backups must have, on the Backups page and for backup keygen (12 to 128, 12 by default). A made-up passphrase and one that opens an existing backup are never judged by it.
help.Backups__MaxUploadMb: The largest backup an administrator may upload on the Backups page (1024 by default). Copying a file into the backups folder always works; give it a name that does not start with tankstat-backup-, or retention counts it as one of the app's own.
help.Logging__LogLevel__Default: The least important lines written for every category not listed here.
help.Logging__LogLevel__Tankstat: The app's own lines: Information shows what an operator looks for, Debug every ordinary change by id.
help.Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft_AspNetCore: The web server's lines. Never below Warning: its request lines hold the tokens of password reset links.
help.Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft_EntityFrame: The database layer's lines; Information writes every SQL command.
help.Logging__LogLevel__System_Net_Http_HttpC: Outgoing requests, such as those to the photo reading server; Information writes a line per request.
help.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: The collector or backend telemetry goes to, such as http://otel-collector:4317 (gRPC) or http://otel-collector:4318 (HTTP). Empty (the default): nothing is sent. An address outside your network sends every trace, metric and log line there.
help.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL: grpc (the default, usually port 4317) or http/protobuf (usually port 4318), as the endpoint expects.
help.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS: Sent with every export, as key=value pairs separated by commas, such as a backend's API key (x-api-key=...). It is never shown back.
help.OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: The name the telemetry is filed under in the backend; tankstat by default.
help.Telemetry__TraceDatabase: Also sends a span for every database command, with its SQL text. Beta: EF Core's instrumentation is a pre-release, and its masking of the values written into a command can miss one, so a value could reach the backend; what people type is sent as parameters, which are never exported. Off by default, and only with an endpoint.
